subject: CFA with missing="FIML" produces intercept parameter intercepts?

messages.author: bec3b6c763e426c0
messages.subject: CFA with missing="FIML" produces intercept parameter intercepts?
parts:
I am running a one-factor CFA model using a ML estimator, but I added an option to handle missing data using FIML (missing="FIML"). This is to use all available data rather than do list-wise deletion when data are missing in a case. 
However, running the model with this option results in the three intercepts being estimated, which I don't want to do.
When I remove the missing="FIML" option, the output does not estimate the intercepts.
Could someone please explain to me why this is happening and if there is a way to use FIML without having to estimate the extra intercept parameters?
Thanks in advance - my code is below. 

## Create the LV
LV <- 'F1=~x1+ x2+ x3 + x4'

## Fit model to data
fit.LV <- cfa( LV   , data = mydata, estimator="ML", missing="FIML") 

## Output
summary(fit. LV   , fit.measures = T, standardized = T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: CFA with missing="FIML" produces intercept parameter intercepts?
parts:
lavaan's implementation of FIML requires a mean structure, but it will be saturated by default, so it does not affect your results (same covariance-structure parameter estimates, same fit and df).
